title: RTInfer: Real-Time Inference of Multiple DNNs on Edge GPUs
claim: Existing schedulers force deadline-driven preemption that wastes memory and sacrifices accuracy under bursts; a calibrated variant recovers accuracy while meeting deadlines.
layout: 3 panels: task list left, two stacked timelines center, bar chart right
description: The left column lists four DNN tasks ordered by priority from High to Low, shown as a red-orange to pale-orange to green gradient. Each task has a small network icon, a bar divided into early-exit points (Exit 1–4), an arrival marker A and a deadline d. Three real-time tasks and one best-effort task are shown. The center holds two stacked memory-address versus time timelines. Colored blocks mark each task's execution and preemption under a dashed red Memory Budget line. Panel (a) shows the baseline Pantheon, which leaves gaps and cuts tasks off at early exits. Panel (b) shows PC-Pantheon, where tasks are packed more compactly and run to later exits. Arrows mark arrivals and deadlines. The right panel (c) is a bar chart of accuracy for t1, t2 and t3 with three bars each (original, Pantheon, PC-Pantheon). Pantheon's bars are visibly lower than the originals, and PC-Pantheon recovers part of the loss.

abstract: While edge GPUs are increasingly used for latency-critical DNN tasks, limited resources often fail to meet strict real-time (RT) requirements under concurrent workloads. Existing preemption and early-exit mechanisms often underutilize GPU resources through single-task queuing and sacrifice excessive accuracy during task bursts. To address this, we propose RTInfer, a novel system that enables concurrent RT task execution while balancing throughput and accuracy. RTInfer integrates an accuracy-calibrated lightweight variant co-optimization to generate efficient models, a memory-layout-aware scheduler to mitigate fragmentation during preemption, and an on-demand loading strategy to minimize host-to-GPU latency. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that RTInfer outperforms state-of-the-art methods by reducing average deadline miss rate (DMR) from 32.8\% to 0\% and improving accuracy by up to 56.5\%.
